facts.claim: The U.S. FDA has issued dedicated guidance for implanted brain-computer interface devices intended for patients with paralysis or amputation; the final guidance was issued on May 20, 2021 and remains part of the FDA’s neurological-device regulatory framework.
facts.source_title: Implanted Brain-Computer Interface Devices for Patients with Paralysis or Amputation — FDA

facts.claim: Neuralink’s PRIME study is an active, recruiting first-in-human early-feasibility study evaluating the safety and functionality of its N1 Implant and R1 surgical robot in people with tetraparesis or tetraplegia. The ClinicalTrials.gov record was last updated January 9, 2026 and lists estimated enrollment of 15 participants.
facts.source_title: PRIME: An Early Feasibility Study of a Precise Robotically Implanted Brain-Computer Interface — ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06429735

facts.claim: Paradromics completed the first human implantation of its Connexus BCI on June 17, 2026, as part of the FDA-approved Connect-One early-feasibility study, which is designed to evaluate speech restoration and computer control for people with severe motor impairment.
facts.source_title: Paradromics and University of Michigan Complete First Connexus BCI Implantation

facts.claim: A 2026 Nature Medicine study reported nearly two years of independent, at-home use of an intracortical BCI by a man with ALS: more than 3,800 hours of use, over 180,000 communicated sentences, and 99.2% word accuracy in a prompted task.
facts.source_title: Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain–computer interface for speech and cursor control — Nature Medicine

facts.claim: A 2025 Nature study demonstrated an instantaneous brain-to-voice neuroprosthesis in a man with ALS using four implanted arrays containing 256 microelectrodes; the system synthesized intelligible speech and allowed real-time modulation of intonation and short melodies.
